newsitem.title: USA: NY Gov extends pacts with 5 Native American tribes.
newsitem.headline: NY Gov extends pacts with 5 Native American tribes.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki Thursday said interim pacts on the sale of gasoline and cigarettes with five Native American tribes were extended by 30 days to give the negotiators time to finish a tax compact.
He noted a similar extension was agreed on Wednesday with a sixth tribe, the Oneida Nation, while talks are continuing with the Senecas, St. Regis Mohwaks and the Poospatuck.

The agreements the state hammered out with the tribes set up a licensing and stamping program that means the Native American nations get revenues for their members but the pacts do not impose state taxes, Pataki explained in prepared remarks. The tribes agreed to raise the price of cigarettes sold on their reservations as a first step in getting "an acceptable level of parity," he said previously.

A group of convienence stores had sued the state to force it to collect taxes on gasoline and cigarettes because they said the reservations' tax-free status had unfairly boosted their sales, and a state judge ruled in their favor.

Pataki, while saying he wanted to work cooperatively with St Regis Mohawks, did not reveal whether he would agree to suspend a blockade as the tribe requested, noting: "We suspended implementation of the regulations for 27 months, time and again, and we're encouraged that they have sent back a responsible look at it."
The interim pacts were extended on Thursday with the Shinnecock and the Haudenosaunne, which include the federally recognized Onondaga, Tuscarora, Tonawanda Seneca and Cayuga Indian nations.

The Pataki Administration has been under considerable pressure from the tribes that are holding out, as a rally on Sunday outside Buffalo on the section of the state Thruway that runs through the Cattaraugus reservation turned violent, and 12 state troopers were injured.
